audit_scope.description: Batch 10 covers BLAKE2F precompile validation and execution, MODEXP precompile, EIP versioning semantics (EIP-7577), and fork activation criteria. Focus is on precompiled contract security, gas economics, and protocol governance mechanisms.

misclassified_entities.reason: Contract calling BLAKE2F is internal EVM execution, not external to EL. Smart contract bytecode executes within the system boundary.
Calling contract or EOA invoking precompiles is internal EVM state, not external entity.

trusted_external_entities.name: Users/Smart Contracts via Transactions - Precompile Calls
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: EVM CALL opcode to precompile addresses
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users and smart contracts invoke precompiled contracts (BLAKE2F at 0x09) via transactions or internal CALL operations. Input data is untrusted and must be strictly validated for length (exactly 213 bytes for BLAKE2F) and parameter values (final flag must be 0 or 1). Malformed input could cause execution failures or gas calculation errors.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Proposers via Consensus - Timestamp for Fork Activation
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Post-merge, CL validators set block timestamps that trigger timestamp-based fork activations. Channel is authenticated via Engine API, but validators could manipulate timestamps within consensus rules (up to drift limits) to affect fork timing. EL must use timestamps for deterministic fork activation while trusting CL to prevent manipulation.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peers via DevP2P - Blocks for Fork Rule Validation
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers send blocks that must be validated under correct fork rules based on block number (pre-merge) or timestamp (post-merge). Malicious peers could send blocks invalid under current fork or valid under wrong fork. EL must correctly identify applicable fork and apply corresponding validation rules.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Input data to BLAKE2F must be exactly 213 bytes. First 4 bytes are rounds (big-endian U32), bytes 4-67 are h (8x8 bytes), bytes 68-195 are m (16x8 bytes), bytes 196-203 are t_0, bytes 204-211 are t_1, byte 212 is f (final flag, must be 0 or 1). Any deviation causes InvalidParameter exception. Gas is GAS_BLAKE2_PER_ROUND * rounds, which must not cause out-of-gas.

Block timestamp >= fork activation timestamp triggers fork activation. Timestamp validity is guaranteed by CL consensus. EL must evaluate ByTimestamp.check(block.header.timestamp) to determine if fork rules apply. Malicious timestamp manipulation is prevented by CL, but EL must handle edge cases at exact activation boundary.

EL must determine applicable fork by evaluating all fork criteria in order (ByBlockNumber < ByTimestamp < Unscheduled). For received block, extract block_number and timestamp, evaluate fork criteria, select latest activated fork, apply that fork's validation rules. Invalid blocks under applicable fork must be rejected.
